full_text_records.title: Two-fluid and magnetohydrodynamic modelling of magnetic reconnection in the MAST spherical tokamak and the solar corona
full_text_records.pages_read: PDF 1–16: all body, methods, results, discussion, figures/captions, references; no internal appendix
full_text_records.figures_checked: Direct PDF visual: Eq.1–5 and definitions (pp3–4), Fig.3 (p7), relaxation equations/Figs.4–8 (pp9–10,13–14); remaining figure captions read in full text
full_text_records.model: 2D Cartesian / axisymmetric toroidal Hall MHD plus separate preliminary two-temperature extension; separate analytical Taylor relaxation model is not species heating simulation
full_text_records.closure: Hall ue=vi-di*j/n; scalar pe; ion viscous heating, electron resistive and hyperresistive heating, anisotropic heat conduction. Initially printed total-pressure Eq.5 does not itself resolve Ti/Te; preliminary independent temperature equations described on pp5–7 but not printed in full.
full_text_records.geometry_initial_boundary: Two detached parallel-current flux ropes and strong toroidal guide field; toroidal case includes confining vertical field. Relaxation model fixes total helicity and toroidal flux.
full_text_records.parameters: n0=5e18 m^-3, L0=1 m, B0=0.5 T, initial Ti=Te=10 eV, di=0.145; eta=1e-5, nui=1e-3, kappae_parallel=0.1, kappai_perp=1e-7; Fig.3 etaH=1e-8.
full_text_records.numerics: HiFi framework and predecessor Stanier2013/Stanier2014 thesis; heating figure's grid/time/convergence not reported here. No independent simulation reproduced.
full_text_records.finding: Fig.3 preliminary two-temperature toroidal run gives downstream double ion-temperature peaks from viscous heating, order-keV ion peak, spatially distinct electron heating dominated by hyperresistive current gradients. Relaxation theory predicts magnetic energy available and its Bp^2-like scaling, but explicitly not the species partition/spatial pattern.
full_text_records.limitation: Hyperresistivity is a free model parameter and sets electron heating localization; scalar finite closure lacks kinetic distributions. Comparison to MAST is qualitative/preliminary, ion peak differs from lower-drive experiments, central versus hollow Te/plasmoid explanation tentative. No universal Qi/Qe.
full_text_records.assessment: Direct evidence that an extended two-temperature Hall model can compute local Ti,Te and budget under specified dissipative closures; not a parameter-free validation of physical irreversible partition.

full_text_records.title: Slow shocks and conduction fronts from Petschek reconnection of skewed magnetic fields: two-fluid effects
full_text_records.version: arXiv:1006.0441v1 (2010-06-02); local regenerated title page says draft May 29 2018; not a new publication
full_text_records.pages_read: PDF 1–45 including all Sections 1–7 and references; no internal appendix
full_text_records.figures_checked: Direct PDF visual: Eqs.4–7 (p10), Eqs.14–18 (p12), Figs.4–7,9–14 (pp17,19,20,24,26,28,30,32,35,37). Remaining figures/captions read in text.
full_text_records.model: 1D quasi-neutral common-velocity two-temperature collisional hydrodynamics for parallel shocks, mapped into prescribed Petschek skew-field reconnection outflow; not a self-consistent Hall reconnection simulation.
full_text_records.closure: ni=ne=n, vi=ve=v follows the current-free shock reduction; inertialess electron electric field balances electron pressure. Separate Ti/Te with classical ion viscosity, ion/electron conduction, interspecies Coulomb heat exchange. Maxwellian intra-species closure; no direct X-point heat.
full_text_records.geometry_initial_boundary: Reconnection assumed instantaneous at t=0; mirrored shock tube with incoming v=-Mi, n=1, Ti=Te=0.3 at remote side, v=0 and zero gradients at center; initial v=-Mi*tanh(s/lambda), lambda varied.
full_text_records.parameters: Mi=2.4,3.6,5 examples; lambda=1–500 ion viscous mean-free-path units; Pr_e=0.013, Pr_i=0.33, f1=0.019; transport proportional to T^(5/2), collision frequency n*Te^(-3/2). T normalization cs1^2=10kBT1/(3mi). Skew angle roughly <=120 degrees for clean hydro reduction, discussion approximate extension <=150 degrees.
full_text_records.numerics: Steady ODE shooting based on eigen-directions and time-dependent hydrodynamic integrations. Detailed mesh/order/time-step/convergence not reported in the read version; prior kinetic shock comparisons cited but not reproduced.
full_text_records.finding: Conduction front, ion viscous subshock and long ion-cooling region separate spatially; early Ti overshoots equilibrium, delayed electron heating and conduction redistribute energy. Far-downstream equilibrated Rankine-Hugoniot state can agree with single-temperature model although transient local temperatures differ strongly. Large initial shear width can reverse local Ti-Te ordering. Heat exchange/cooling region grows strongly with Mach number.
full_text_records.limitation: Ion heat flux reaches/exceeds free-streaming and viscous pressure positivity criterion can fail during transient strong shock, so classical ion closure is unreliable precisely near some heating layers; electron flux remains much smaller in studied cases because electrons are heated indirectly. Model lacks X-point direct heat, kinetic tails, changing flux-tube cross section, antiparallel limit, and self-consistent Hall field.
full_text_records.assessment: Strong counterexample to any claim 'two fluid cannot study separate heating': it resolves a conditional collisional thermalization chain. It does not calculate a universal reconnection Qi/Qe or validate collisionless entropy production; no direct laboratory comparison.

direct_citations.relation: kinetic pickup heating offered as alternative beyond fluid shock closure

No source data/code or independently supplied supplement

full_text_records.title: Two-temperature effects in Hall-MHD simulations of the HIT-SI experiment
full_text_records.version: OSTI author accepted manuscript, 35 pages: article pp1–18 and enlarged/repeated figures pp19–35. Unreviewed November 2020 erratum exists.
full_text_records.pages_read: PDF 1–35: all body, methods, results, conclusions, references and appended repeated/enlarged figure pages; no internal appendix.
full_text_records.figures_checked: Direct PDF visual: Eq.1–13/Table I (pp3–4), Figs.2–4 (pp7–9), Figs.5–13/scan results (pp11–17); overview of appended repeated images pp19–35. Key Ti/Te map and heating power plot inspected. Some noncentral scan figures reviewed at contact-sheet scale.
full_text_records.model: 3D two-temperature Hall MHD in PSI-Tet and NIMROD; separate ion/electron temperatures; simple enhanced electron-inertia current-time derivative in Ohm law.
full_text_records.closure: Scalar pressure, Spitzer resistivity, constant isotropic ion viscosity, Braginskii anisotropic conduction, Coulomb exchange; Ohmic heat assigned electrons, viscous heat ions. Electron temperature advected/compressed with ue in accepted Eq.4. Artificial density diffusivity. Pressure compression is reversible work, not automatically entropy production.
full_text_records.geometry_initial_boundary: HIT-SI flux conserver driven by two phase-shifted AC helicity injectors. PSI-Tet includes full injector volume; NIMROD axisymmetric vessel with injector-mouth BC. Wall B.n=J.n=0, no-slip velocity, prescribed n/T; NIMROD has resistive exterior and imposed inflow at mouths.
full_text_records.parameters: f_inj=14.5,36.5,53.5,68.5 kHz; flux0.5 mWb/current8 kA; n_wall=0.75e19 m^-3, T_wall=3 eV baseline; nu=550 m²/s, D=250 m²/s; effective mi/me=100 (f_me=36.72; scan18.36–73.44); di about8 cm, mouth14 cm. Wall T1,3,10 eV and density/diffusivity scans.
full_text_records.numerics: PSI-Tet 103887 tetrahedra,2.8 cm elements,third order,effective9 mm vs artificial de12 mm; implicit Crank–Nicolson dt<=40 ns,typical10 ns high frequency. NIMROD1.8 cm poloidal fourth-order cells,11 toroidal modes; prior convergence cited. Artificial density-diffusion contribution about3–5% inferred power; low-D limit not converged.
full_text_records.finding: Independent Ti/Te changes simulated temperature and density relative to 1T; at higher drive frequency ions hotter than electrons, spatial maps have similar large-scale structure but different temperature levels (Fig.4 caption); modeled viscous ion and Ohmic electron sources plus species conduction/losses explain conditional local and global budgets. Authors report qualitative agreement with ion Doppler and preliminary Thomson data, explicitly not close quantitative experiment validation.
full_text_records.limitation: A full circuit drive, neutral/atomic/radiative losses, realistic wall conditions and improved viscosity remain missing. Temperature depends on boundary and D; no D-insensitive convergence. Geometry differs between solvers. An erratum (10.1063/5.0032632) is confirmed by Crossref but correction text inaccessible; no unchecked corrected-equation or precise partition claim made.
full_text_records.assessment: The most direct retrieved self-consistent Hall-MHD example of separate species thermal evolution, including spatial Ti/Te and budget channels. Evidence is conditional on closure/drive/wall model and recorded accepted version; not a universal heating ratio and not a pure reconnection-local budget isolated from the injectors.

full_text_records.title: High-order two-fluid plasma solver for direct numerical simulations of plasma flows with full transport phenomena
full_text_records.version: arXiv1812.11237v1 2018-12-28, accepted for 2019 article; catalog previously used preprint year2018
full_text_records.pages_read: PDF1–44: entire text and references including Appendix A plasma transport, B quasineutrality, C single-fluid limits.
full_text_records.figures_checked: Direct visual Eq15–19 (p11), identical-temperature restriction (p16), Figs1,3,4,7,9,10,11 (pp18,21,25,27,35), AppendixA EqsA1–A9,A15–A19 (pp31,33). All other figures/captions read in text.
full_text_records.model: Reduced quasineutral massless-electron Braginskii two-fluid equations with full anisotropic transport; all four actual tests impose Ti=Te, equivalent to a single-temperature extended Hall system.
full_text_records.closure: Chapman–Enskog near-Maxwellian collisional transport: species viscosity/heat flux, current and thermal friction, Ohmic heating, +/-Q_delta; scalar pressures plus constitutive viscous stresses. No independent kinetic heat-flux closure.
full_text_records.geometry_initial_boundary: 1D periodic small-amplitude Alfven/whistler; Dirichlet Brio-Wu shock tube; 2D Harris-like reconnection box12.8x25.6, conducting x/periodic y, no initial guide field.
full_text_records.parameters: Wave NX384, domain9.6,m2–30,amplitude1e-5. Shock Rei6.3e3/2.3e4,Rem~1e12,di/L1e-6. Reconnection di/L1,Rei124–850 (additional1029 convergence case),Rem58–890; principal Rei426/Rem112. Reference L~10 m,n~1e15 m^-3 for reconnection, varied T/B to attainable transport parameters.
full_text_records.numerics: CFDNS sixth-order nondissipative compact finite differences with physical viscosity/diffusion, no high-order filtering. Shock finest NX40960/122880; observed orders6.14/6.08,Re_grid~2.3 criterion for studied cases. Reconnection principal convergence256x512,finest768x1536,order6.58; Rei1029 converges384x768; threshold~2.6. Specific time-step/time-integration details not supplied in this paper; prior CFDNS methods cited.
full_text_records.finding: Full two-species heating equations can be written and numerically regularized using physical transport, with high-order grid convergence and local common-temperature heating maps. Saturated reconnected flux/time becomes weakly sensitive for their large tested Rei/Rem.
full_text_records.limitation: SectionIV PDF16 explicitly sets Ti=Te for every demonstrated problem and eliminates independent ion-energy evolution; no species heating partition computed or validated. Collisional closure can be inappropriate at coronal diffusion-layer scales; matching reconnected flux does not validate kinetic thermalization or heat partition. Infinite-c and zero-electron-inertia approximation excludes electron scales.
full_text_records.assessment: Useful method/convergence evidence, not a direct two-temperature heating-result paper. Report authors' broad claim of collisionless applicability as their assessment limited by the actual flux test, not an established proof for heating.

full_text_records.title: The scaling of the ion heating and electrostatic potential in spherical tokamak
full_text_records.version: Watermarked PREPRINT—IAEA-FEC2025 manuscript; no peer-reviewed journal version verified
full_text_records.pages_read: PDF1–8 all manuscript, methods, results, summary, references; no appendix.
full_text_records.figures_checked: All Figs1–7 visually inspected on pp2–6 and Eq1 p2 / heating definition p7 checked directly. Key graph axes/offsets read from image.
full_text_records.model: Experiment plus analytic scaling plus VPIC kinetic simulation. Introduction mentions two-fluid Hall-MHD, but no independently specified Hall equations, run, grid or result is reported; NOT counted as a Hall heating simulation.
full_text_records.closure: Experimental Ti inferred from neutral Doppler tomography using claimed rapid ion-neutral relaxation; floating potential converted to plasma potential using Eq1 and probe Te. PIC full distribution, reduced mass ratio; downstream heating diagnostic printed as mi/2*(<v²>-<v²>0), with no explicit mean-flow subtraction or 3D temperature conversion.
full_text_records.geometry_initial_boundary: TS-6 merging in cylindrical vessel radius.375m,length1.44m;288 Doppler sightlines. VPIC two-plasmoid coalescence Ay=B0*lambda*ln[cosh(z/lambda)+.4*cos(x/lambda)], uniform guide field; x periodic, y/z conducting and particle-reflecting.
full_text_records.parameters: Experiment Brec~.014–.03T,guide~.15–.16T typical; guide-ratio scan~4–9; hydrogen/argon comparison. PIC mi/me=200,omega_pe/Omega_ce=2,Ti0=Te0,200particles/cell/species,t~50/Omega_ci. Grid/time text prints delta x0.3lambda_D and delta t0.3/omega_pe without relation sign; actual mesh counts and scan convergence not reported.
full_text_records.numerics: VPIC named; no grid/particle/mass-ratio convergence study or separately specified Hall simulation. Reduced geometry/reflecting boundaries acknowledged for potential amplitude difference.
full_text_records.finding: Authors report quadrupolar potential correlated with downstream Doppler-temperature pattern, field/guide trends, and PIC potential amplitudes within20% of experiment; a proposed potential scaling is DeltaPhi∝Brec*Bg. These are manuscript claims, not an independent confirmation of universal irreversible heating or Qi/Qe.
full_text_records.limitation: No electron/ion heat-partition budget. Temporal correlation alone does not establish unique causality. Fig3 potential fit has large intercept427V and Fig4 scan substantial uncertainty; claims of zero-offset universal product scaling exceed shown evidence. Definition of PIC DeltaTi may include bulk flow. Eq1 floating-potential conversion insufficiently justified; raw diagnostics/code not available. No basis to equate simulated potential with floating-potential diagnostic without synthetic-probe model.
full_text_records.assessment: Recent experimental/kinetic boundary evidence; useful because it directly shows why title/introduction 'Hall' and20% agreement cannot be read as validation of Hall-MHD species heating. Do not promote speculative universal/reactor extrapolation statements.
